data.title: Invesco QQQ ETF Loses 6% as Chip Stocks Pull the Tech Basket Lower
data.description:
Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq-100 index (NDX), closed 5.67% lower on Friday at $608.45. Chipmakers Nvidia (NVDA), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Micron (MU), and Broadcom (AVGO) dragged the fund down the most. Each stock fell by more than 12% in Friday's trading. This came as tech shares sold off for a second day.

Again, Anthropic's record Nasdaq debut on Thursday failed to reassure investors about the AI trade. Overall, Friday marked another bruising session for the U.S. stock market.

The companies highlighted above rank among the QQQ's top holdings. Some of the stocks traded slightly higher in after-hours trading.

Why Chip Stocks Sold Off on Friday

Beyond general market pressure, company-specific updates also weighed on chip stocks Friday.

  • Nvidia shares (NVDA) plunged 14.01% to $125.53. This followed reports that the U.S. securities watchdog is investigating the chipmaker's accounting practices. This marks an escalation in the controversy facing the company. It follows a Chinese spy scandal that forced the dramatic exit of its longtime CEO, Jensen Huang, last week.
  • Advanced Micro Devices shares (AMD) dropped by 13.25% to $424.39. Shares in the chipmaker tumbled for a second day after a short-seller report. The report alleged that Chinese server maker IEIT Systems continued to receive updated AMD firmware despite being placed on the U.S. trade blacklist in March 2025. The report also flagged AMD's financial exposure to its AI clients through leases and loan guarantees.
  • Micron shares (MU) plunged 13.89% to $594.51 as worries about Big Tech debt could impact spending. Nvidia's ongoing leadership crisis also contributed to the sell-off.
  • Broadcom shares (AVGO) dropped by 12.19% to $304.41. This followed reports that Google (GOOGL) has cut 2027 shipments of its TPU 8i chip series by about 20%.
data.author: Solomon Oladipupo

data.title: CoreWeave Stock (CRWV) Forecast – Here's Why Wells Fargo Remains Bullish Despite Ongoing Selloff
data.description:
CoreWeave (CRWV) stock has declined more than 36% over the past month amid worries about the neocloud company's high debt to fund AI infrastructure buildout. Moreover, concerns about the sustainability of the AI trade, customer concentration risk, and the Nvidia (NVDA) turmoil have also weighed on investor sentiment. Nevertheless, Wells Fargo analyst Michael Turrin remains bullish on CRWV stock and reiterated a Buy rating with a price target of $115.

Following meetings with management, the analyst said that he was "encouraged by continued signs of improving AI monetization & a credible product story building." Despite ongoing volatility, Turrin believes that the fundamentals are still intact.

Wells Fargo Is Optimistic About CoreWeave's Growth Prospects

Among the key takeaways from management meetings, Turrin noted that CoreWeave has dual product priorities – a leading AI infrastructure platform and rapidly expanding software businesses, including Managed Inference, which now exceeds $250 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). He also highlighted the company's expanding enterprise presence, with more than 10% of the Fortune 500 as customers, including industrials (CRWV's biggest bet), FinServ (more than 10% of backlog), and telecom.

Furthermore, Turrin said that demand continues to outsize supply, driving higher monetization rates. CoreWeave is now generating $20 million to $25 million per megawatt for deals with a duration of 4-5 years, while short-duration contracts are exceeding $40 million and are expected to become a larger share of the mix.

Overall, pricing gains are more than offsetting higher costs and financing expenses. Turrin added that CoreWeave is seeing demand that is ten times its remaining 2027 capacity and multiple times its 2028 capacity. The analyst also noted that CoreWeave has 170,000 GPUs up for renewal in 2027, which it expects to generate about $4 billion in ARR at current rates without additional funding. Also, delays at rival neocloud providers could further increase the value of CRWV's existing infrastructure.

Turrin also noted that CoreWeave expects to meet most of its funding needs through delayed-draw term loans (DDTLs), which it believes will be widely available, as about 75% of its requirements are supported by investment-grade or enterprise customers. Also, CRWV is returning to a higher mix of deals with prepayments (expects over 70% of future deals to include prepayments) at a much smaller discount than the prior 10% to 15% on average selling price.

Is CRWV a Good Stock to Buy?

Overall, Wall Street has a Moderate Buy consensus rating on CoreWeave stock based on 20 Buys, six Holds, and three Sells. The average CRWV stock price target of $104.70 indicates 165% upside potential.

data.title: OKLO Stock Is Down 71% YTD — Why This Five-Star Analyst Says to Jump In
data.description:
Shares of U.S. small modular reactor producer Oklo (OKLO) have fallen by 71% since the start of the year. Still, five-star Guggenheim analyst Joseph Osha upgraded the stock from Hold to Buy on Friday. Osha also set a $38 price target, suggesting about 93% upside. Osha said Oklo's third-quarter earnings update left him optimistic.

Why Guggenheim Upgraded Oklo Stock to Buy

During the quarter, Oklo reported revenue of $1.86 million, above the consensus of $1.01 million. Its loss of $0.22 per share was narrower than analysts' consensus estimate of $0.27.

Osha believes that Oklo continues to meet key milestones across its nuclear power, isotope, and fuel businesses. This progress is moving the SMR producer closer to launching commercial operations, Osha noted.

Notably, Oklo achieved "first criticality" with its Aurora powerhouse in August. This means the reactor successfully started up. It also means that the plant achieved a self-sustaining nuclear fission chain reaction.

Guggenheim Says Oklo Is Trading at a Discount

According to Osha, another reason for the upgrade is the sell-off in Oklo shares. The analyst noted that Oklo has fallen by 80% from its January peak. He believes the current share price undervalues the company and its advantages.

Osha sees Oklo's current share price as offering "an opportune entry point for investors to step into a business that continues to build commercial momentum and is beginning to transition from development to construction and real-time operations."

Guggenheim Is Bullish on Oklo's Commercial Progress

Meanwhile, the Guggenheim analyst is also bullish on Oklo meeting targets on schedule in the race to go commercial. He pointed to the quick completion of Groves I, Oklo's nuclear test reactor.

"To date, we don't think OKLO has been given enough credit for the accelerated completion of Groves I — being as the project was [completed] entirely on their own and well ahead of schedule," Osha noted. "Because of that success, another reactor is now already underway and targeting first commercial isotope delivery as soon as next year."

Who Is Joseph Osha?

As a five-star analyst, Osha ranks No. 1,384, placing in the top 11% of the 12,000-plus analysts tracked on TipRanks.

He boasts a 46% success rate. His ratings have generated an average return of 8.80% for investors.

Is Oklo Stock a Good Stock to Buy?

Across Wall Street, Oklo's shares remain a Moderate Buy based on analysts' consensus rating. This breaks down into nine Buys and six Holds assigned over the past three months.

However, the average OKLO price target of $48.64 implies about 145% upside ahead (see OKLO stock forecast here).

data.title: Microsoft Tightens Employee Pay Rules as AI Competition Heats Up
data.description:
Software giant Microsoft (MSFT) is changing how it rewards employees in its Azure cloud business, with top performers set to receive more stock awards. Meanwhile, workers who receive lower performance ratings will have formal meetings with their managers, according to a memo reviewed by Bloomberg. The changes come as Microsoft faces growing pressure to get more work done while spending billions of dollars on artificial intelligence.

Arun Ulagaratchagan, executive vice president of Azure, explained in the memo that employees who deliver exceptional results should receive greater rewards. However, managers must also be honest with workers whose performance falls short of expectations. A Microsoft spokesperson said that the changes will help employees better understand what is expected of them and receive more direct feedback from their managers.

The company has not disclosed how much additional stock its top employees will receive. Still, the changes show that Microsoft wants to make a stronger connection between employee pay and individual performance.

That approach comes as Azure continues to grow. In Microsoft's latest quarter, Azure revenue increased by 48%, while its total cloud revenue grew by 30% to $63.9 billion. Overall company revenue rose by 19% to $92.3 billion.

However, supporting that growth is expensive. Microsoft spent $45.2 billion on capital expenditures during the quarter, largely to expand the computing infrastructure needed for its AI services. As those costs increase, the company is looking for ways to get more value from its workforce.

Microsoft Continues to Make Changes to Its Workforce

The new Azure pay rules follow several other moves to reduce employee costs. In October, Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to approximately 60,000 workers, which made up more than one-quarter of its global workforce of 223,000 employees. The company also eliminated about 4,800 positions in July. The latest changes suggest that Microsoft is placing more importance on employee productivity.

Other technology companies have adopted similar approaches. In February, search giant Google (GOOGL) offered voluntary buyouts to some employees in its business division. An executive told staff that they needed to fully support the company's AI strategy and be prepared for a faster work environment.

Is MSFT Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, TipRanks data shows that analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on MSFT stock. This is based on 35 Buys and four Holds assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. Furthermore, the average MSFT price target of $632.48 per share implies 29.9% upside potential. (See MSFT Stock Forecast).

data.title: "Buyout Carnage" Sends Skydance Stock (NYSE:SKYD) Down Again
data.description:
Entertainment giant Skydance (SKYD) has been engaging in cost-cutting measures of late, in a bid to pare down its roughly $80 billion debt load. And to that end, it has offered numerous buyout packages to get employees to leave voluntarily. The buyouts have especially hit CBS News hard, noted a report from the New York Post, with some calling it "buyout carnage." Skydance stock dropped nearly 2% in the closing minutes of Friday's trading. Skydance has seen a 59.57% loss in its share price over the past year.

Why Not Just Fire Them?

One staffer actually referred to the buyout spree as an "extinction-level event," and the report also noted that the foreign desk was being hit especially hard. Staffers are departing everything from 60 Minutes to the CBS Evening News, and the Washington and London bureaus are also getting hit quite a bit. Though, interestingly, even as the impact is being felt, the buyouts represent a comparatively small proportion of what was offered. The report noted that less than 10% of the CBS News employees who were offered the voluntary packages actually took them.

The London desk was said to be offered particularly generous buyout packages, mostly due to labor laws in the United Kingdom. There also seems to be a growing body of concern that says if they do not take the buyout offers now, they may be thrown out outright later. Further there is some impact on morale as, at CNN, the New York bureau has been seeing a lot of buyout offers get accepted. One insider called it a "brain and production drain," but Skydance may simply be clearing house here.

Two Words: Trunk Scripts

Joe Ravitch, founder of the Rain Group, recently offered up some insight on how Skydance will be able to meet its stated goal of 30 films released theatrically every year. Ravitch seems convinced that the only way to do this will be to turn to international releases. A Variety report went on to note that such films would require "big investments" to accomplish.

Ravitch appears to have forgotten the lessons of the 2010s, in which the direct-to-video boom was running at its fullest. In those days, film releases were at a fever pitch, with even small studios like Anchor Bay Releasing turning out multiple titles per year. The notion that Skydance would be required to go international in order to fill a quota of 30 in a year seems to ignore virtually every small-scale studio—from Shout Factory to Lionsgate (LION)—who released a whole lot more than that in the course of a typical year when all they were doing was stamping DVDs. There are enough scripts sitting in the trunks of amateur screenwriters–trunk scripts–right in the United States to make going abroad largely unnecessary.

Is Skydance a Good Stock to Buy Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Hold consensus rating on SKYD stock based on five Buys, five Holds and five Sells assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. The average SKYD price target of $9.50 per share implies 52.37% upside potential.

data.title: U.S. Market Melts Down as Nasdaq Gives Up Gains on the Year
data.description:
It was another brutal day for the U.S. market as stocks sold off across the board, ending a difficult week for investors. The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite index shed 1,261 points or 5.28% on Nov. 20 and turned negative for the year, registering a 1% decline for 2026. The other two major indices in the U.S., the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average, each entered correction territory, defined as a drop of 10% or more from recent highs.

The S&P 500 traded down 2.2% on Friday, while the blue-chip Dow lost 352 points, or 0.7%. There were few places for investors to hide as stocks got slammed in most sectors. For the week, the Dow declined 6%, its worst performance since April 2025 when U.S. President Donald Trump announced his sweeping tariffs. The S&P 500 dropped 7% for the week, and the Nasdaq plunged 8% over the last five trading sessions.

Anthropic's Stock Falls

The stock of artificial intelligence (AI) firm Anthropic (ANT) fell sharply on Nov. 20, a day after its highly anticipated initial public offering (IPO). Anthropic lost 12%, giving back most of the 17% gain achieved on its first trading day, according to data from Dow Jones. Chipmakers Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Nvidia (NVDA) fell 11% and 7%, respectively, as the AI trade continues to unwind.

There had been hope that Nvidia's earnings on Nov. 17 and Anthropic's IPO on Nov. 19 would revive AI stocks. But now, the market looks to be on the verge of capitulation as investors grow increasingly worried about the AI infrastructure buildout and seek safety in lower volatility names. Shares of Walmart (WMT) gained 3% to end the week, while Costco Wholesale's (COST) stock added 2% as investors turn defensive in the wake of the market selloff.

Stock Winners & Losers

Stocks that fared best on the day include:

  • UnitedHealth (UNH)
  • The Home Depot (HD)
  • T-Mobile (TMUS)
  • General Mills (GIS)
  • Humana (HUM)

Stocks that badly underperformed on Nov. 20 include:

  • SanDisk (SNDK)
  • Coherent (COHR)
  • Micron Technology (MU)
  • Western Digital (WDC)
  • Bloom Energy (BE)

data.title: Nvidia vs. Alphabet: One AI Stock Is a Bargain, the Other Raises Red Flags, Says Investor
data.description:
It's been a year Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) investors would prefer to forget. Despite delivering strong financial results, both companies have found themselves caught in a Wall Street sell-off driven by a near-perfect storm of political, regulatory, and financial concerns. The Democrats' Blue Wave election victory has raised fears of tougher restrictions on AI development and data center construction, while the scandal surrounding Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, followed by his resignation, has shaken confidence in one of the industry's most influential leaders.

And the problems don't end there. China's regulatory tensions have weighed on semiconductor stocks, while repeated attempts to stabilize the market have failed to stop the selling. Even Anthropic's blockbuster IPO, initially seen as a potential turning point for the tech sector, failed to lift investor confidence, with the stock plunging just one day after its debut. Add mounting losses at investment funds, persistent inflation, and hawkish Federal Reserve commentary pointing toward higher interest rates, and investors have plenty of reasons to remain cautious.

But as legendary investor Warren Buffett has long argued, periods of widespread fear can also create opportunities to buy outstanding companies at discounted prices. The challenge, of course, is distinguishing between stocks that have become genuinely undervalued and those whose falling prices reflect deeper problems.

That brings us to Nvidia, Alphabet, and investor Gil Rotstein, who believes the recent sell-off has created a buying opportunity in one AI giant but exposed serious concerns about the other. After examining both companies, he sees a bargain in one stock and growing financial risks in its rival.

Starting with Nvidia, Rotstein believes investors are overlooking the chipmaker's underlying financial strength as concerns surrounding its former CEO and Washington's investigations dominate the conversation.

"Don't be a fool and think Washington will let it drown," Rotstein said.

Rotstein believes Nvidia's importance to the broader tech industry and the enormous amount of computing infrastructure being built worldwide make it unlikely that Washington would take actions that could seriously damage the company. In his view, policymakers have strong incentives to protect a leading supplier of the hardware powering the AI revolution.

Valuation is another important consideration. According to Rotstein, Nvidia trades at less than 10 times expected fiscal 2028 earnings, compared with 28.5 times for AMD and 17.6 times for Broadcom. He also points to the company's remaining $227.3 billion share repurchase authorization, which could provide additional support for existing investors.

There are risks, particularly from regulatory investigations and competition from custom-designed processors. However, Rotstein believes the potential rewards outweigh those concerns, especially given Nvidia's ability to maintain strong profitability across its integrated hardware and software offerings.

Ultimately, Rotstein rates Nvidia shares a Buy, viewing the gap between its operational performance and depressed valuation as an opportunity for patient investors. (To watch Rotstein's track record, click here)

Alphabet presents a more complicated picture. Rotstein previously supported the Google parent's investment prospects, but its latest quarterly results have prompted him to reconsider whether the company's enormous AI expenditures are creating enough value for investors.

"That is why I'm downgrading Alphabet to Hold," Rotstein noted.

The decision follows a second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow, with Alphabet reporting a $9.1 billion shortfall in Q3. Capital expenditures reached $51.4 billion, exceeding the $42.3 billion generated from operating activities. Meanwhile, the company has raised billions of dollars through debt and equity offerings as it continues its costly infrastructure expansion.

This represents a significant departure from Alphabet's historical approach, when profits from Search and other established operations could finance new investments while leaving substantial resources available for share repurchases.

To be clear, the company's growth remains impressive. Third-quarter revenue climbed 25% to $127.6 billion, while Google Cloud sales more than doubled to $30.7 billion. Nevertheless, Rotstein is concerned about slowing advertising growth, potential pressure on future profitability, and the absence of clear evidence that the latest spending commitments will generate adequate returns.

He also sees limited valuation protection; at approximately 25 times adjusted earnings, Alphabet does not appear especially inexpensive compared with other tech giants, particularly given its complicated financing requirements.

For Rotstein, the company remains a formidable competitor in artificial intelligence, but its financial trajectory needs to improve before he would consider becoming bullish again.

What Does Wall Street Think About Nvidia and Alphabet Stocks?

So, what does Wall Street think? Analysts aren't giving up on either AI giant. Nvidia has earned a Moderate Buy consensus rating, with 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell. Its average price target of $232.59 points to a potential gain of ~82%. Alphabet looks even more popular among analysts, with 30 Buys and just 4 Holds, giving it a Strong Buy consensus rating. However, its average target of $398.50 implies a smaller, though still attractive, 48% upside. (See NVDA stock forecast or GOOGL stock forecast)

data.title: AMD: Unfairly Maligned, or Right Where It Belongs?
data.description:
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) fell 7.7% on Thursday due to a negative report from Hunterbrook Media. Investors are asking, is this report credible?

What is Hunterbrook? There is Hunterbrook Media, which reported Thursday that products created by AMD are in the possession of backlisted companies in China.

There is also Hunterbrook Capital LP, a related hedge fund based in New York. That fund has opened a short position in AMD. Hunterbrook Capital is apparently hedging this trade with a long position in what it describes as "a basket of comparable securities." 

Individuals can also hedge their investments, as explained here.

Best of the Bunch?

Despite Thursday's selloff, AMD is holding up better than many names in the semiconductor sector. The stock is still up 118% year-to-date. Compare this to competitor Nvidia (NVDA), which is down 22.7% for the year.

After a huge bullish run, we closed half of our AMD position late last year. We reduced the position by half once again this past July. We exited the remainder of our AMD shares on November 6, as reported here. We currently have no position in AMD.

SEC Exemption

According to an April 2026 SEC filing, Hunterbrook Capital LP manages about $119 million across its funds. Because it has less than $150 million under management, it qualifies as an Exempt Reporting Advisor (ERA). An ERA is exempt from full SEC registration and can only advise private funds. 

The fact that Hunterbrook Capital LP is small may reduce its credibility in the eyes of some. Meanwhile, AMD has denied any wrongdoing.

Casting Doubt

Several new outlets cast doubt on the Hunterbrook report. CNBC's Jon Fortt challenged the accuracy of the report, saying it "didn't make sense." 

After the close, the U.S. Commerce Department further muddied the waters, noting that as of May 2026, it approved the sale of 879,000 AI chips to buyers in China. As of this writing, AMD has not commented on the Commerce Department statement.

Past Performance

We know that past performance is not indicative of future results, but just the same, we wanted to explore some of Hunterbrook's prior shorts.

Hunterbrook Capital announced a short position in UWM Holdings (UWMC), a wholesale mortgage lender, in April 2024 (point A). At the time, the stock was trading near $6.50. 

The stock subsequently rallied. A trader that shorted UWMC in April could have lost nearly 50% by late August (point B).

Hunterbrook Media claimed that UWM Holdings engaged in questionable business practices. Hunterbrook Capital hedged its short position in UWMC with a long position in Rocket Mortgage.

UWM Holdings trades near $1.13 today (point C), losing nearly 87% from its August 2024 peak. Hunterbrook's allegations against UWM Holdings may not be responsible for that decline, as the mortgage sector has been battered by high interest rates.

Bloom Energy

Bloom Energy (BE) manufactures and installs solid oxide fuel cell systems, which are used to provide on-site power in data centers. 

In July of this year, Hunterbrook announced that it shorted the stock (point A), accusing Bloom of using third-party companies to obscure its supply chain. This was allegedly done to cover up the use of companies based in China as part of that supply chain. 

Bloom Energy responded by describing the accusations as false and misleading.

In less than one month, shares of Bloom Energy fell nearly 40% to the $160 area (point B). During that month, the S&P 500 rose slightly, so we can't blame the market. Despite a subsequent rally, the stock fell back to that area and is currently trading near $170 (point C). 

In this case, it does seem that Hunterbrook's report had an impact on the stock. However, Bloom Energy's more recent decline could be attributed to a general rotation away from AI and data center stocks. 

Bottom Line

It's never been conclusively proven that any of the allegations made by Hunterbrook are either true or false. That said, AMD will be a litmus test for Hunterbrook, defining our perception of that company. 

If the allegations are false, the stock should bounce back. Hunterbrook may have just created a buying opportunity for AMD bulls. If the stock recovers, shorts — including Hunterbrook Capital — will take a loss. 

However, even if that's the case, AMD exists within a weak sector, which exists within a weak market. It might be the best of its group, but right now, that's not good enough. We're staying flat.

data.title: Why SpaceX Stock (SPCX) Is Falling Today – November 20, 2026
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) shares are falling today as the rocket and satellite company faces new problems with its planned $74 billion AI infrastructure investment. Indeed, Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes has asked officials to delay a December 9 vote on the company's proposed $50 billion AI data center. Meanwhile, officials in Texas have refused to move forward with discussions about a tax break for a separate $24 billion SpaceX project.

According to Bloomberg, Mayes wants Cochise County officials to wait until state and federal agencies finish reviewing the Arizona project. She is concerned that the facility could put too much pressure on the region's electricity and water supplies.

The concern comes from the size of the project. SpaceX plans to build the facility on nearly 750 acres of land, and it could eventually require six gigawatts of electricity. That would equal about 20% of Arizona's current electricity output capacity. To help meet that demand, SpaceX says it plans to spend about $3.6 billion on upgrades to the local power network. The company also claims that its partnerships with local electricity providers could lower electricity bills by up to 20%.

SpaceX has also tried to address worries about water usage. It plans to cool its equipment with air instead of a system that uses water through evaporation. According to the company, the facility would eventually use about as much water per year as 20 to 30 Arizona households.

However, Mayes wants regulators to examine these claims before the project receives approval. She has also scheduled a community meeting for December 3, six days before the planned vote.

SpaceX Faces Another Setback in Texas

The situation in Arizona comes just days after SpaceX faced a similar problem in Texas. On November 17, Cameron County officials voted 3-2 against holding a public hearing to consider a tax break for the company's $24 billion project near Brownsville.

That project would cover approximately 444 acres and include an AI data center powered partly by a natural gas power plant. SpaceX estimates that it could create 500 jobs and initially add $13.8 billion in taxable property value to the county.

The company had proposed a 10-year agreement that would reduce its property taxes. In exchange, SpaceX would make negotiated payments to the county. It argued that this would give local officials a more predictable source of tax revenue.

Following the vote, SpaceX warned that the county's tax revenue could change more from year to year as its equipment loses value over time. The company said that it plans to continue discussions with local officials about how the project could benefit the area's economy.

Furthermore, the average SPCX price target of $263.83 per share implies 103.2% upside potential. (See SPCX Stock Forecast).

data.title: Ford Stock (NYSE:F) Makes Gains in Canada; Share Prices Gain Too
data.description:
Legacy automaker Ford (F) is a surprising hit in Canada, based on how much support it has found from the Canadian government to keep its operations running in the country. New Super Duty pickups are starting to roll off the lines in Oakville, Ontario, backed up by a substantial amount of Canadian taxpayer money. Ford shares gained fractionally in Friday afternoon's trading. Ford has also seen a 9.43% loss in its share price over the past year.

Back in Action

The plant at Oakville was recently retooled, and rather substantially, based on some current reports. Today was the official relaunch of the site as the Oakville plant prepared to start producing F-Series Super Duty pickups. Two years of construction went into this retooling operation, and no small amount of Canadian taxpayer money, noted a report from Yahoo! Finance.

The report noted that Ottawa put up $464.5 million to support the retooling operation and keep the plant's workforce alive during the reconstruction process. Reopening brought out several Canadian dignitaries, including Premier Doug Ford, as well as federal Industry Minister Melanie Joly, and Unifor's national president, Lana Payne. This also comes not long after Ford set up a new collective bargaining agreement that included a set of wage increases and additional preservation for job security, which is set to last for the next 3 years.

Perhaps a Bit Too Far

A report from Ford Authority, meanwhile, gave us a look at a Ford Festiva that got pretty impressively retooled itself. Originally, the Festiva was designed as basic travel, with no frills and a comparatively low point of entry budget-wise. But a vehicle released as "no frills" might as well be called "blank slate" to others, and so a recently spotted Ford Festiva that was converted into what can only be called a terrestrial helicopter makes a certain kind of sense, though perhaps, a very deranged kind.

The vehicle in question was spotted roaming the streets of Chalfont, Pennsylvania, and indeed looks like a military helicopter of some sort, complete with top-mounted propeller, a set of turbines that clearly do not work, and a complete tail section. Granted, this is little more than an unusual-looking vehicle, but the fact that these kinds of modifications could be done with a Festiva suggests that Ford's "no boring cars" ethos could be better left in the hands of car buyers.

Is Ford Stock a Good Buy Right Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on F stock based on six Buys and six Holds assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. The average F price target of $15 per share implies 33.57% upside potential.
